implementation_notes: The query object is assembled through CriteriaBuilder: createQuery() returns a CriteriaQuery, Path/Root references plus cb.equal/ge/and/or compose a Predicate tree (the API uses Predicate rather than Expression<Boolean> because Java generics are not compatible with varargs), and the provider renders it for the configured dialect with bound parameters. What replaces the classic hand-written query class is the criteria metamodel, which makes dynamic string JPQL obsolete; a different DSL (for example jOOQ) stays justified when SQL-level control matters more than provider portability, and a static named query when the query never varies.
pitfalls: CriteriaQuery is mutable and owned by the EntityManager that created it: it must not be cached or passed across persistence contexts or threads.
Attribute names are strings: use the generated static metamodel (Customer_.status), otherwise renames are invisible to the compiler.
Because building goes through cb, a session must exist before the query can even be composed - composition and execution stop being separable.
